newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to seek early broker fee deregulation - paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan to seek early broker fee deregulation - paper.

text.p: A Ministry of Finance panel will propose that brokerage commissions are fully deregulated in 1999, a year earlier than the securities industry had recommended, the business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Tuesday.

The Securities and Exchange Council is to meet on Tuesday to decide on the schedule for implementing reforms in the securities market, and will submit its final report to the government on Friday, the paper said.
The council will also propose abolishing the licencing of brokerages, and instead recommend the introduction of a registration system in 1998/99, the paper said.
The panel will also recommend that the autumn of 1999 be the deadline for removing a rule barring banks' securities units from dealing in the cash stock business, the paper said.
A ministry official declined to confirm the newspaper report, saying that the panel's report has not yet been finalised.
